title: Make the price sync apply the whole feed

blocks.text: The catalog service applies the supplier's price feed every night and republishes the catalog when any price changed. The feed is not trusted: some lines name no SKU, and some carry a price of zero or less. Both kinds must be skipped, and neither may stop the sync.
`CatalogSync` already reads the feed, applies a single change and reports. Finish the two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/CatalogSync.java`:

items: `acceptable(change)`: whether a line of the feed may be applied, as its comment defines it;
`step(changedSoFar, change)`: one step of the sync, called once per line, in order.

blocks.text: When you're done, every acceptable line reaches the catalog, no other line touches it, and `sync` returns `true` exactly when some price changed. About two lines in total.

cases.says: a single acceptable change is applied and reported, and a feed that changes nothing reports no change
once one change has changed the catalog, the changes after it are still applied
the sync reports a change made anywhere in the feed, not only by its last line
a change with a price that is not positive never reaches the catalog
a change with no SKU is skipped without an exception, and the rest of the feed is applied

origin.section: && and || Skip Their Right Operand; & and | Always Evaluate Both

concepts: && and || skip their right operand when the left decides the result, so && can guard a null check; & and | evaluate both and throw on the null.
A call on the right of || or && is skipped once the left decides, so changed = changed || apply(x) stops applying after the first change.
